sprint-2026-10-31-1.title: §1.3 · Trigonometric functions
sprint-2026-10-31-1.detail: Finish the whole lesson: radians, unit circle, identities, graphs and transformations. Write the standard-angle values from memory.

sprint-2026-10-31-2.title: §2.2 · Limits and limit laws
sprint-2026-10-31-2.detail: Learn graphical/numerical limits, limit laws and algebraic simplification. The assigned 65a/66a exceptions are compulsory.

sprint-2026-10-31-3.title: Independent practice · complete today’s 30 questions
sprint-2026-10-31-3.instructions: Finish the listed sets without solutions open. Mark each as independent, helped or incorrect; redo every helped/incorrect question.
sprint-2026-10-31-3.detail: The first two blocks include guided attempts. Use this block to complete and check their exact lists; do not count the same question twice.

sprint-2026-10-31-4.title: Exit check · trigonometry and limits
sprint-2026-10-31-4.instructions: Reattempt 5 of today’s questions with no notes: 2 trig and 3 limits, including one from 65a/66a. Target at least 4/5; use remaining time to repair errors.

sprint-2026-11-01-1.title: Chapter 3 · vector repair
sprint-2026-11-01-1.detail: Review components, unit vectors, addition, scalar/vector products and signs. Chapter 3 is not assumed mastered.

sprint-2026-11-01-2.title: Chapter 4 · finish the entire lesson
sprint-2026-11-01-2.instructions: Work one example for each: 2D position/velocity/acceleration, projectile motion, uniform circular motion, tangential/radial acceleration, relative velocity and relative acceleration.
sprint-2026-11-01-2.detail: Projectiles need practice; relative motion and every later Chapter 4 section still need learning. Draw the reference frame before using equations.

sprint-2026-11-01-3.title: Chapter 4 · independent problem set
sprint-2026-11-01-3.detail: Finish the Chapter 3 list in this block too. Check vector direction, units and reference frames; use solutions only after a written attempt.

sprint-2026-11-01-4.title: Exit check · vectors, projectiles and relative motion
sprint-2026-11-01-4.instructions: Redo 4 missed questions, including a projectile and a relative-motion question. Explain each diagram and reference frame aloud; aim for 4 independent solutions.

sprint-2026-11-02-1.title: Chapter 3 · math functions, strings and objects
sprint-2026-11-02-1.instructions: Write 4 programs from a blank file: degree/radian converter, distance calculator, character-code converter and formatted receipt.
sprint-2026-11-02-1.detail: Complete Chapter 3, including imports, strings, escapes, conversion, methods and formatting. Run each program on at least 3 inputs.

sprint-2026-11-02-2.title: Chapter 4 · selections
sprint-2026-11-02-2.instructions: Write 4 programs: maximum of 3 numbers, grade classifier, leap-year test and quadratic-root classifier.
sprint-2026-11-02-2.detail: Finish comparisons, Boolean operators, if/elif/else, nested decisions and common selection errors. Test equality and boundary cases.

sprint-2026-11-02-3.title: Chapters 3–4 · tracing and debugging
sprint-2026-11-02-3.instructions: Answer 20 practice questions: 10 from Ch. 3 and 10 from Ch. 4. Predict output on paper before running code; correct all eight programs.
sprint-2026-11-02-3.detail: Use the chapter banks in the linked practice app. Prioritize every unanswered question before repeating a correct one.

sprint-2026-11-02-4.title: Exit check · rebuild and test
sprint-2026-11-02-4.instructions: From blank files, rebuild the receipt and grade classifier in 40 minutes; spend 20 minutes correcting. Each must pass normal, boundary and invalid-input checks you define.

sprint-2026-11-03-1.title: Foundations · PDF pp. 1–30
sprint-2026-11-03-1.instructions: Write 12 short question/answer cards covering engineering, science, work/job/profession, needs, aptitudes and career choice.
sprint-2026-11-03-1.detail: Read every slide in this range. Recall the definition before looking at the slide; keep the Arabic terminology used in class.

sprint-2026-11-03-2.title: Profession and ethics · PDF pp. 31–65
sprint-2026-11-03-2.instructions: Write 12 scenario cards: public safety, competence, honest reporting, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, credit and engineering thinking.
sprint-2026-11-03-2.detail: Finish all slides through page 65. For each rule, give a concrete example of following it and violating it.

sprint-2026-11-03-3.title: Practice · first two foundations lessons
sprint-2026-11-03-3.instructions: Answer all questions in “مفهوم الهندسة والعلم” and “المهنة وأخلاقيات المهندس”. Then answer your 24 cards without the PDF.
sprint-2026-11-03-3.detail: Use only the foundations lessons; research methods belong to the later final-exam plan.

sprint-2026-11-03-4.title: Exit check · definitions and ethics
sprint-2026-11-03-4.instructions: Randomly select 10 of your cards and answer closed-book. Target 8/10; correct every missing definition or scenario and retest.

sprint-2026-11-04-1.title: §2.4 · One-sided limits
sprint-2026-11-04-1.detail: Study both sides separately and decide whether a two-sided limit exists. All four exceptions 43–46 are compulsory.

sprint-2026-11-04-2.title: §2.5 · Continuity
sprint-2026-11-04-2.detail: Cover continuity at a point and on intervals, discontinuities, piecewise parameters and the intermediate value theorem.

sprint-2026-11-04-3.title: Independent practice · complete both lists and revisit limits
sprint-2026-11-04-3.instructions: Finish the 29 listed questions, then §2.2: 7, 15, 23, 35, 57 (5 additional questions). Correct every failed attempt.

sprint-2026-11-04-4.title: Exit check · 6 questions without notes
sprint-2026-11-04-4.instructions: Redo §2.4: 43–46 and your two hardest §2.5 questions. Aim for 5/6 independent solutions, with reasons for each continuity claim.

sprint-2026-11-05-1.title: Prerequisite repair · Chapters 1–2
sprint-2026-11-05-1.instructions: Solve 6 short textbook practice problems: power/signs, Ohm’s law, KCL, KVL, series/parallel and Wye–Delta; one of each.
sprint-2026-11-05-1.detail: Select the first unsolved Practice Problem for each topic in the textbook. Show your own circuit labels and equations.

sprint-2026-11-05-2.title: Chapter 3 · ordinary nodal analysis
sprint-2026-11-05-2.instructions: Solve 5 nodal circuits from the section’s examples and adjacent Practice Problems. Cover current sources and a source connected to ground.
sprint-2026-11-05-2.detail: Choose a reference, label voltages, write KCL, solve, and verify each result with a branch-current or power check.

sprint-2026-11-05-3.title: Chapter 3 · supernodes
sprint-2026-11-05-3.instructions: Solve 5 supernode circuits: floating voltage sources, a dependent source, and a mixed ordinary-node/supernode case. Use section examples and adjacent Practice Problems.
sprint-2026-11-05-3.detail: Write both the supernode KCL and voltage-source constraint. Attempt each worked example with its solution covered.

sprint-2026-11-05-4.title: Exit check · two complete circuits
sprint-2026-11-05-4.instructions: Pick 1 ordinary-node and 1 supernode circuit you needed help with; solve both from blank paper in 60 minutes, then check KCL and source constraints for 30 minutes.

sprint-2026-11-06-1.title: Chapter 5 · learn the complete chapter
sprint-2026-11-06-1.instructions: Draw free-body diagrams for horizontal motion, inclines, connected bodies, friction and equilibrium. Work one example of each.
sprint-2026-11-06-1.detail: Cover all chapter sections. Choose axes before resolving forces; distinguish mass, weight and normal force.

sprint-2026-11-06-3.title: Chapter 5 · applications set
sprint-2026-11-06-3.detail: For every problem, include the diagram, component equations, units and a physical reasonableness check.

sprint-2026-11-06-4.title: Exit check · Newton’s laws
sprint-2026-11-06-4.instructions: Redo 3 missed Ch. 5 questions without notes, then 1 previously missed Ch. 4 relative-motion question. Correct the force diagrams before checking algebra.

sprint-2026-11-07-1.title: Chapter 5 · while and for loops
sprint-2026-11-07-1.instructions: Write 3 programs: sentinel-controlled average, multiplication table and sum of a numerical series.
sprint-2026-11-07-1.detail: Finish range, counters, accumulators, sentinel values, break/continue, and termination conditions.

sprint-2026-11-07-2.title: Chapter 5 · nested loops and problem solving
sprint-2026-11-07-2.instructions: Write 3 programs: prime checker, greatest common divisor and a nested-loop number pattern. Run 3 test cases per program.
sprint-2026-11-07-2.detail: Trace the changing state on paper. Include zero/one and boundary cases where relevant.

sprint-2026-11-07-3.title: Practice · loops and selection repair
sprint-2026-11-07-3.instructions: Answer 20 Ch. 5 practice questions and redo 5 Ch. 4 questions you got wrong. Debug and finish all six programs.

sprint-2026-11-07-4.title: Exit check · loop program from memory
sprint-2026-11-07-4.instructions: Rebuild sentinel average and prime checker from blank files in 40 minutes; spend 20 minutes testing boundaries and explaining why each loop terminates.

sprint-2026-11-08-1.title: §2.6 · Infinity and asymptotes
sprint-2026-11-08-1.detail: Learn infinite limits, end behavior and vertical/horizontal asymptotes. Do all 63–68 except the dominant-term part, as the course plan requires.

sprint-2026-11-08-2.title: §3.2 · The derivative as a function
sprint-2026-11-08-2.detail: Learn difference quotients, derivative functions, differentiability versus continuity, and derivative graphs.

sprint-2026-11-08-3.title: Independent practice · complete both lists
sprint-2026-11-08-3.instructions: Finish the 35 listed questions, then §2.5: 7 and 19 (2 extra questions). Redo helped attempts; write an asymptote and derivative error checklist.

sprint-2026-11-08-4.title: Exit check · infinity and differentiation
sprint-2026-11-08-4.instructions: Redo 3 missed infinity questions and 2 derivative-definition/graph questions without notes. Aim for 4/5; correct all misses.

sprint-2026-11-09-1.title: Engineering disciplines · PDF pp. 66–95
sprint-2026-11-09-1.instructions: Build a comparison table from these slides: each discipline, its work, tools and examples. Write 10 short recall questions.
sprint-2026-11-09-1.detail: Read all slides in the range and connect each specialty to a concrete application.

sprint-2026-11-09-2.title: Finish foundations · PDF pp. 96–122
sprint-2026-11-09-2.instructions: Write 10 more questions covering the remaining technology/history/design topics exactly as presented; reproduce every process diagram from memory.
sprint-2026-11-09-2.detail: Finish the file. Reopen pages 1–65 for a 20-minute retrieval check before starting practice.

sprint-2026-11-09-3.title: Practice · full foundations bank
sprint-2026-11-09-3.instructions: Finish all questions in “التخصصات الهندسية والتكنولوجيا”, then redo every incorrect item from the first two foundations lessons.
sprint-2026-11-09-3.detail: Do not count the research-methods lessons as midterm scope. The local bank is supplementary practice, not a recovered instructor quiz.

sprint-2026-11-09-4.title: Mock · all engineering foundations
sprint-2026-11-09-4.instructions: Answer 30 mixed foundations questions closed-book in 45 minutes, then correct for 45 minutes. Target 24/30; retest each error with an explanation.

sprint-2026-11-10-1.title: Chapter 3 · mesh and supermesh
sprint-2026-11-10-1.instructions: Solve 4 mesh circuits and 3 supermesh circuits using covered examples/adjacent Practice Problems; include a dependent-source case.
sprint-2026-11-10-1.detail: Finish every remaining Chapter 3 method, including choosing nodal versus mesh, inspection and the chapter’s circuit-analysis workflow.

sprint-2026-11-10-2.title: Chapter 4 · linearity
sprint-2026-11-10-2.instructions: Solve 3 linearity/scaling problems from §4.2 examples and Practice Problems. State the assumption behind each proportionality.
sprint-2026-11-10-2.detail: Complete the saved midterm boundary at linearity. Later Chapter 4 methods stay in the final-exam schedule.

sprint-2026-11-10-3.title: Mixed review · Chapters 1–3
sprint-2026-11-10-3.instructions: Answer all 10 textbook Ch. 3 Review Questions (3.1–3.10), then solve 1 Wye–Delta, 1 nodal and 1 supernode problem from your error log.

sprint-2026-11-10-4.title: Mock · circuits midterm scope
sprint-2026-11-10-4.instructions: In 75 minutes solve 5 circuits: basic laws/power, nodal, supernode, mesh/supermesh and linearity. Spend 45 minutes correcting; require a valid equation set for all 5 and 4 correct final results.

sprint-2026-11-11-1.title: Chapter 6 · functions and parameters
sprint-2026-11-11-1.instructions: Write 4 functions from scratch: maximum, prime test, GCD and unit conversion. Test return values with at least 3 calls each.
sprint-2026-11-11-1.detail: Finish function definitions/calls, parameters versus arguments, return versus print, local scope, default/keyword arguments and the remaining chapter topics.

sprint-2026-11-11-2.title: Chapter 6 · integrated program
sprint-2026-11-11-2.instructions: Build a menu-driven calculator with functions, input validation, selections and a repeat-until-exit loop. Test each operation and exit behavior.
sprint-2026-11-11-2.detail: Complete the remaining chapter examples. No copying during the independent rebuild.

sprint-2026-11-11-3.title: Practice · Chapters 1–6
sprint-2026-11-11-3.instructions: Answer 24 mixed questions: 4 per chapter. Trace by hand before execution and explain the cause of every error.

sprint-2026-11-11-4.title: Mock · programming fundamentals
sprint-2026-11-11-4.instructions: 60 minutes closed-book: 10 tracing/debug questions plus 2 programs (one loop/selection and one function). Use 60 minutes for testing and repairs; target 8/10 and both programs passing 3 cases.

sprint-2026-11-12-1.title: Chapter 6 · finish all applications
sprint-2026-11-12-1.instructions: Work examples for circular motion, banked curves, vertical circles, accelerated frames, resistive forces and terminal speed where covered in the chapter.
sprint-2026-11-12-1.detail: Study the entire chapter. Distinguish inward net force from a new physical force; draw real forces first.

sprint-2026-11-12-3.title: Prerequisite check · Chapter 2 and error log
sprint-2026-11-12-3.instructions: Serway Ch. 2: 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 35 (7 questions). Prioritize any you cannot start; recall the Ch. 3–5 diagrams and equations on one page.

sprint-2026-11-12-4.title: Mock · Physics Chapters 2–6
sprint-2026-11-12-4.instructions: 75 minutes: 6 questions from your sets (1 Ch. 2, 1 vectors, 1 projectile, 1 relative motion, 1 Newton’s-laws application, 1 circular motion). Use 45 minutes to correct; target 5/6.

sprint-2026-11-13-1.title: §3.3 · Differentiation rules
sprint-2026-11-13-1.detail: Finish power, sum, product and quotient rules; include higher derivatives and the lesson’s applications.

sprint-2026-11-13-2.title: §3.5 · Trigonometric derivatives
sprint-2026-11-13-2.detail: Learn the trig derivative formulas, radians, tangent lines and the section’s limit/application examples.

sprint-2026-11-13-3.title: Independent practice · finish today’s 31 questions
sprint-2026-11-13-3.instructions: Finish both lists; rebuild a one-page formula sheet from memory and redo the weakest 3 questions from earlier calculus days.

sprint-2026-11-13-4.title: Mock · Calculus §§1.1–3.5
sprint-2026-11-13-4.instructions: 75 minutes: 12 mixed questions (1 each from §§1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 3.2; 2 each from §§3.3 and 3.5). Use 45 minutes to correct; target 10/12 and retest all misses.
